transcript.text: Bottom rack on my Beko DVN05320W isn't getting clean and I've noticed the lower spray arm has a crack along one side and wobbles. Do I just need a new arm?

**Probably yes.** A cracked lower spray arm is very likely your main problem, and it's a cheap, easy part to replace. Check a few things while it's out, though, so you don't buy the arm and still have the problem.

## Why the crack matters
The arm spins because water jets out of angled nozzles. A crack lets water escape where it shouldn't, which:
- drops the pressure at the nozzles, so the bottom rack gets weak spray
- often stops the arm spinning properly, so whole areas get missed

A wobble on top of that makes it worse, since the arm can drag, tilt, or catch on items.

## Before ordering, check these
1. **Remove the arm.** On most Beko models it pulls straight up or unscrews/unclips from the centre hub. Look at the **centre hub/bearing** on the arm. If that's cracked or worn oval, it explains the wobble.
2. **Check the mount it sits on** (the stub in the base of the tub). If that's loose, cracked, or the seal is damaged, a new arm may still wobble.
3. **Clean the filters.** Twist out the cylindrical filter and the flat mesh under it, rinse them, and scrub off any grease. Clogged filters cause poor bottom-rack cleaning too.
4. **Clear the nozzles** on the old arm with a cocktail stick. This tells you whether blockage was also part of it.

## Getting the right part
- Find the **model and serial/product number** on the sticker on the edge of the door or the side of the tub. Beko sometimes changes parts between production runs of the same model name.
- Order from Beko's official spares site or a reputable parts supplier, and match it by model/product number, not just by photo.
- Lower spray arms are usually inexpensive and fit without tools.

## After fitting
Spin the new arm by hand. It should turn freely and sit level without rocking. Run a hot empty cycle to check.

**If the new arm still wobbles,** the problem is the mount/bearing in the sump, which is a more involved repair. You might call Beko or an engineer at that point, especially if the machine is still under warranty.

Had the arm out. Crack is about 5cm along one arm and water would spurt out of it. Hub/bearing looks fine, it spins but wobbles. Filters were clean, and a couple of the holes had limescale blocking them, the rest were clear. Not sure how to check the mount. I don't know the part number, so which arm do I order?

## Finding the right arm

I don't want to guess a part number, because getting it wrong means a wasted order. Here's how to get the right one:

1. **Look at the old arm.** Many arms have a part number moulded into the plastic, often on the underside near the hub. If there's a long number (Beko numbers are usually around 10 digits), search that number directly.
2. **Get the product number from the rating plate.** It's on the sticker on the edge of the door or the side of the tub. Note the **model (DVN05320W) and the product/serial number**. Beko sometimes uses different parts across production runs of the same model.
3. **Search by model.** On Beko's official spares site, or a parts retailer like eSpares or Partmaster, enter the model and pick "lower spray arm". If several arms come up, use the product number to choose between them.
4. **Compare against the old arm** before ordering: length, number and layout of nozzles, and the shape of the centre fitting.

If you're unsure, Beko customer service can confirm the part from your product number.

## Checking the mount

With the arm off:
- **Look at the stub** in the base of the tub where the arm sits. Check for cracks, chips, or a worn or missing seal or ring.
- **Wiggle it gently.** It should feel firm with no rocking. Some movement in a separate retaining nut or collar is fine if it's seated properly.
- **Refit the old arm and watch it.** Does the wobble come from the arm flexing, or from the whole hub rocking on the stub?

Since your hub looks fine, the likely cause is that the crack has weakened the arm so it flexes and spins unevenly. Spray escaping from the crack can also push it off balance. A new arm should fix both. If a new arm still rocks, the mount is the problem.

## The limescale

Blocked holes point to hard water, so it's worth preventing:
- Keep the **salt reservoir** topped up, and check the **water hardness setting** matches your area (your water supplier's website will tell you).
- Use **rinse aid**.
- Run a **dishwasher descaler** or hot empty cycle with citric acid every month or two.

Until the new arm arrives, it's fine to keep using the dishwasher. The bottom rack just won't clean as well.
Ok, I'll check the rating plate on the door edge. The model is DVN05320W, and I can read out the product code from the plate if you need it. Is that what I should use to pick the arm?

Yes, use the product code alongside the model number. It identifies your machine's exact production version, which matters when Beko has used more than one arm for the same model.

You don't need to read it out to me. I can't look it up in Beko's parts database, so I couldn't confirm the right arm from it. Use it directly:

1. **On Beko's spares site or a parts retailer**, search by model (DVN05320W). If they ask for the product code, or list several lower arms with different code ranges, pick the one that matches yours.
2. **If the listing doesn't mention product codes** and there's only one lower spray arm for your model, that's almost certainly the one.
3. **Check it against the old arm** before ordering: length, nozzle layout, and the centre fitting.
4. **If it's still unclear**, give the model and product code to Beko customer service or the retailer's support team. They can confirm the part number.

Keep the old arm until the new one is fitted, so you can compare them side by side.
